dek: UKMTO: an 'unknown projectile' hit a tanker 11nm west of Bukha (Bukha), Oman, sparking a fire that was extinguished; vessel at anchor, all crew safe, no environmental impact. Attacker NOT identified by UKMTO.

sections.what_happened: UKMTO: an 'unknown projectile' hit a tanker 11nm west of Bukha (Bukha), Oman, sparking a fire that was extinguished; vessel at anchor, all crew safe, no environmental impact. Attacker NOT identified by UKMTO. Separately, UKMTO logged a Tuesday projectile strike on a tanker 30nm off Al Faw, Iraq — no casualties, no damage. Brent rose ~0.78% to $109.64 on the news. Separately, IRGC (Sepah News/state TV) claims three tankers hit its mines at the 'illegal' southern route (incl. one with 2M+ barrels, radar off); CENTCOM disputes the mine mechanism, attributes damage to Iranian missiles/loitering munitions (per regional-intel outlet). Houseofsaud analysis: IMF PortWatch — daily tanker transits down 85 -> 4; Kpler throughput -86% (20.8M -> 2.9M bpd Oct 8-11).
sections.what_verified: AFP + iol.co.za + srpske.rs carry the UKMTO Bukha and Al Faw reports with identical details.
sections.what_disputed: Attacker unidentified in the UKMTO Bukha report — any attribution is speculation, hold it. IRGC mine claims are disputed by CENTCOM and unverified independently.
sections.why_matters: The confirmed UKMTO strike near Omani waters is the strongest evidence yet that the waterway war is real and escalating — paired with the 85->4 transit collapse, this is the energy-story spine of the Hormuz thread.
sections.context: Background: Hormuz — NEW in window (Oct 21): UKMTO confirms a tanker struck by an 'unknown projectile' 11nm west of Bukha, Oman (~05:45 ); fire extinguished, at anchor, crew safe. UKMTO also logs a Tuesday projectile strike 30nm off Al Faw, Iraq (no casualties). Brent +0.78% to $109.64. IRGC mine claims vs CENTCOM dispute unresolved.

totw_analysis: Our read: The confirmed UKMTO strike near Omani waters is the strongest evidence yet that the waterway war is real and escalating — paired with the 85->4 transit collapse, this is the energy-story spine of the Hormuz thread. The fault line our audience is arguing over: If neither side will clear the mines and the US won't escort through them, who blinks first on the oil — and what does it cost at the pump?
